scope: The classical alternating comparison for centrally nontrivial amenable actions on finite or countably decomposable infinite semifinite factors, under the stated foundations. Nontrivial inner isotropy and measured-field classification have additional scope.

human_sources.title: Evans–Kishimoto type argument for actions of discrete amenable groups on McDuff factors
human_sources.role: The action-preserving gauge, two-step finite preparation, alternating comparison rows, transported old-cocycle states, and both parity limits are the construction of [Masuda], Theorem 3.1, pp.55–62. Sections 3–4 below spell out the support estimate and a two-term cumulative bound; Sections 5–6 express the two parity cases through one row index. These are explanations of the classical proof strategy. The theorem does not claim a new comparison method.
